interpretation: Both Brier and LogLoss point estimates improve from A0 to A1 and from A0 to A2.
The preregistered support gate fails by a wide margin: only 32 scored walk-forward events, 10 positives, 11 parent groups and 3 inference blocks.
The point estimate is therefore a research clue, not accepted predictive evidence.
Most same-scale pairs have no known preformation coarse background, so the dominant limitation is causal parent-context coverage rather than an observed negative predictive result.
The frozen hierarchy never produced a resolved 2-3T, 3-6T or >=6T background at any evaluated entry opportunity.
Therefore the run did not actually test the economic hypothesis of intermediate-cycle whipsaw versus much-slower dominant trend.
The zero selected-trade result and negative filtered-minus-baseline arithmetic are mechanical consequences of zero coverage, not evidence that top-down context is harmful.
The current B representation fails operational coverage and must not be rerun with post-result threshold relaxation under the same study identity.

overall_adjudication.reason: A shows directionally favorable but severely underpowered development evidence; B produced no resolved contexts and is not an interpretable market test.
do_not: Do not call A predictive support.
Do not call B economically negative or positive from this run.
Do not loosen thresholds or hierarchy requirements inside this frozen study to rescue either gate.
Do not use the baseline trend proxy as trading authority.
Do not promote any publication, trading or production authority.
